title: Copenhagen success, expulsion and the orangutan review
summary: Copenhagen was the greatest success after Berlin, but authorities put them out for taking all the money, and a newspaper called Wooding an orangutan.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Now, but we were a big success. But our greatest success after Berlin was Copenhagen. And that's where we saw the girls before the show, when we came in there, the sophisticated women sitting there with the cigars, you know, the small cigars? And so we used to call them the Great Danes.
Anyhow, this was our greatest success, and that's where pandemonium -- you know we stayed in -- we didn't play but two or three weeks there because they put us out of Copenhagen.
They did?
Because they claimed that we were taking all the money away.
But you were in Copenhagen much later, weren't you?
Oh, yeah.
So we're really ahead of our story.
Yeah, but now, this time, we could have
stayed there four weeks more. But they put us out because --
I mean, did you go to Copenhagen in 1925? After Stockholm?
Yeah, yeah.
I see.
Yeah, that's what I'm talking about, we went to Copenhagen. But the reason why they put us out, not because we were -- we were taking too much of the money out.
Uh hunh.
Everybody was there. That's why I say the greatest success after Berlin was Copenhagen.
Uh hunh.
You see, the Swedish people were all nice and like that, but they didn't have the fire the Danes had. And I'm not saying this because you're from Danish extract, either. (laugh)

I'm saying it because it's the truth. And they made us get out of there, you see? They said, 'You can't take any more money.' And Leonidow almost cried when they put him out. That's where they -- where you saw that article there where they called me an orangutan and all like that. Well they were good people & there, (laugh)
They said in the papers that I translated for you that when it was over and the audience was being
very enthusiastic, you stood center stage, looking very much like an orangutang with a stomach ache. You were taking a bow, right?
That was a fact. Oh, they were a very fine people. And the point of it, they were honest, simply honest. They were honest, eager and simple. And earnest. An earnest honesty, you know what I mean?
Uh hunh.

No put on. It was a great affair. And I only wish I could overlive that again. I'm hoping some day to return to Copenhagen. I just hope I'll have the same success I had then. Because they're very fine people.
